\paragraph{Behavioral and mechanistic analysis of VLAs.}
Behavioral evaluations reveal that current VLAs rely disproportionately on visual input, with language instructions largely ignored during action generation~\cite{grant2026,hou2026,fei2025}.
At the mechanistic level, H\"aon et al.~\cite{haon2025} identified sparse semantic directions in VLA residual streams linked to action selection.
Sparse autoencoder studies have uncovered interpretable features and memorized action sequences~\cite{swann2026,buurmeijer2026}, while probing work has tested for symbolic state representations and emergent world models~\cite{lu2025,molinari2025}.
Fang et al.~\cite{fang2025} showed that fine-tuning erodes general VLM reasoning capabilities.
The closest works are Grant et al.~\cite{grant2026} and H\"aon et al.~\cite{haon2025}.
Grant et al.\ performed a feature-level mechanistic study and found visual dominance; H\"aon et al.\ identified sparse semantic directions linked to action selection, addressing \emph{what} information VLAs encode.
Our analysis is complementary: we address \emph{where} instruction information is redistributed across layers and token positions, decomposing at the token level (identifying the readout as the primary integration site), tracking all 32 layers to reveal a non-monotonic profile, and including trained-vs-untrained factorial controls that isolate fine-tuning effects.

Mechanistic studies have identified sparse semantic directions linked to action selection~\cite{haon2025}, interpretable features and memorized sequences~\cite{swann2026,buurmeijer2026}, symbolic state representations~\cite{lu2025,molinari2025}, and fine-tuning erosion of VLM reasoning~\cite{fang2025}.
